rule: Choosers know pages, not pointers; effectors know pointers and pages but never decide. Pointer literals enter only at the final lowering, as page-table dereferences.

groups.problem: Locating progress, ready, summed, copied, coverage, failure and count words by byte offsets, region offsets or pointer differences.
groups.replacement: Words are pages of the same map. A word layout (tile, frame, channel -> word index) is composed with the page map. The final lowering emits the literal word address.

groups.problem: Turning a pointer or a (buffer, offset) back into region pages, runs or offsets: lease_at, lease_offset, data_off, buffer.contents + offset into ncclMeshRegionRuns.
groups.replacement: No inverse in the compiler. The allocator hands out the page table with the lease. The backing is the image of the map, read from the table. Region offsets are dropped.

groups.problem: Building DMA spans, SGEs, packets and bridge tables from region offsets, backing runs and casts into table memory.
groups.replacement: Specialization at the final lowering. An entry's spans are the image of its page range, coalesced into runs. Cuts are the image's page boundaries joined with the declared logical cuts. Tables are pages of the map written with page indices.

groups.problem: Naming an operand's storage: where, ncclMeshBuffer and ncclMeshBufferSlots fields in chooser records.
groups.replacement: An operand is a page-map value: a page table id and the map invocation -> (virtual page -> physical page), with a position in the operand's logical coordinates. Choosers compose these values. The final lowering specializes them into (region buffer, page index x page bytes) or a pointer literal.

groups.problem: Choosing which storage an invocation uses by hand: % instances, % occurrences, slot x stride, displacement, a fixed generation.
groups.replacement: Lifetime allocation produces the map invocation -> (virtual page -> physical page). The final lowering specializes it per invocation into literal page indices. No modulus remains in any interface.

groups.problem: Knowing when two operands, accesses or steps share bytes, decided by address, byte range or buffer number.
groups.replacement: Intersect the two maps' images. The preimage of the intersection in each operand's logical coordinates is the dependency. Buffer numbers and byte ranges do not take part.

groups.problem: Byte positions of views, segments, rows, frames and pieces inside choosers.
groups.replacement: Compose layouts in the operand's logical (element) coordinates with the page map. Bytes appear only at the final lowering.

groups.problem: Storage for partials, relays, landing areas, generations and an issue's own pages, placed at byte offsets or as numbered buffers.
groups.replacement: These are virtual pages of the function's map with lifetimes. Lifetime allocation assigns their physical pages. Numbered buffers and byte cursors are deleted.

groups.problem: Ordering a write to storage after every reader of its old contents: a landing into bytes a SEND reads, an overwrite after GPU and DMA readers, a cyclic instance taken to mean the same pages.
groups.replacement: Lifetime allocation over the composed map. A physical page takes a new virtual page only after the last reader of the old one in the dependency order. The WAR edge is the preimage of the reused physical page.

groups.problem: Making a Metal buffer, an argument entry or a host pointer for a kernel or CPU leaf.
groups.replacement: Effector: permitted at the final lowering only, with a decided page index as its input. No chooser sees the buffer or the pointer.

groups.problem: Identifying, deduplicating or ordering objects (calls, leases, buffers, words) by their host address.
groups.replacement: Ordinals and page table ids. Equality of storage is equality of page images.

groups.problem: Avoiding a copy by using the send operand's storage as the result's: reading the send buffer in place, landing in recvbuff, complement copies of the ranges no step writes.
groups.replacement: Lifetime allocation decides the sharing. Where each page's last read of the send value precedes the first write of the result, the result's virtual page maps to the same physical page. The complement is the preimage of the result pages no step writes.

groups.problem: Deciding when a returned or owned lease's pages may be reused after their DMA and GPU readers, keyed by address.
groups.replacement: Lifetime allocation keyed by page identity. The retirement ledger lists page tables and their pages, not addresses.

groups.problem: Generated or run-time code that evaluates an address map: div/mod by a layout extent, % instances, mesh_storage_N, mesh_index.
groups.replacement: Specialize at the final lowering: a pointer literal, or base + affine offset, read from the page table.

groups.problem: A chooser reading or writing payload or metadata through a pointer: scalars, identities, copies, fills, progress initial values.
groups.replacement: A data function with page operands, decided by the compiler and run by the effector at the final lowering.

groups.problem: A chooser's headers or translation unit bring pointer types and pointer-yielding calls into scope: Metal.h, nccl.h, mesh-call.h, the bridge's layout.h, the static helpers of nccl-mesh.c.
groups.replacement: Split the headers. A chooser header declares page-map types only. Pointer types and pointer-yielding calls live in the final lowering's header and translation unit, which no chooser includes.

groups.problem: Run-time code that chooses a path, a wait, a threshold or a placement: the kernel scan that picks how far a completed prefix reaches before it publishes.
groups.replacement: The chooser compiles the publication points from the dependency order. The kernel stores at those points and decides nothing.
